parameterHelp.ABORT_EVENT_SENDING_CHANNELS:
To ensure that the device reacts immediately to a new button press, the transmission process of an old button press that is still in progress can be cancelled. For key pairs, e.g. for moving up and down, both selection fields on both key channels should be activated.

When using as a single key, only the selection field with the number of your own key channel should be selected.
parameterHelp.ABORT_EVENT_SENDING_CHANNELS_ACCESS_TRAN:
In order for the device to be able to react immediately to a code that is being received correctly, a transmission of a preceding code that is still in progress can be cancelled.

If a code is valid for more than one channel, the selection fields of the channels should be selected. If the code is only used for one channel, only the selection field with the number of the channel used should be selected.
parameterHelp.ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SIGNAL: With this parameter you can determine whether a failed adaptation run is to be signalled acoustically.
parameterHelp.ACTIVATE_LEVEL_VALUE:
Use this parameter to set the brightness that is switched on for the specified duration after the device is activated by pressing an initial button.

The duration is set using the next parameter 'Switch-on time'.

parameterHelp.AQI_MODE: Different limit values for particulate matter concentrations are set by the national environmental protection authorities. Choose between the national limits of the EU or the USA.
parameterHelp.AUTO_HYDRAULIC_ADJUSTMENT: A hydraulic balancing is performed via the valves, which means that the flow rate at the valves is adjusted so that all rooms heat up at the same rate.
parameterHelp.AUTO_SENSOR_CLEANING:
If the sensor is in measuring mode, automatic cleaning of the air stream path is triggered periodically according to the cleaning interval defined with this parameter. This accelerates the fan to maximum speed for 10 seconds to blow out the dust accumulated inside the fan.

- The measured values are not updated while the fan cleaning is running.
- To disable automatic cleaning, set the interval to 'Not active'.
parameterHelp.BLIND_AUTOCALIBRATION: The automatic calibration run determines how long the shutter/blind needs to move to the desired level. The time for adjusting the slats is not considered and has to be entered manually.
parameterHelp.BLIND_REFERENCE_RUNNING_TIME:
After you have manually changed the movement time value, the CCU has no information anymore on the blind/shutter position. You should therefore perform a calibration run (once completely to up and down). This ensures that the CCU is updated on the blind/shutters exact position.

This applies also to devices with automatic calibration run if you decide to manually change the movement time value.
parameterHelp.BLOCKING_ON_SABOTAGE:

As long as sabotage is triggered via the sabotage contact, incoming codes are not accepted.
parameterHelp.BLOCKING_ON_SABOTAGE_FWI:

parameterHelp.BLOCKING_PERIOD: The motion and presence detection can be deactivated for the time defined here, by linking a push-button or similar to this channel. For normal use indoors, it is accepted that the indoor air will reach the level of fresh outdoor air at least once within a period of one week.

parameterHelp.CYCLIC_INFO_MSG:
Each device sends its status at least one a day. If the parameter **Cyclically status message** is activated, the status is send *additionally* in a time pattern according to the following formula:

*Time for a status message, if the status changes*
**(A+1) x C seconds**

During this interval, only values are transmitted that change slowly, like temperatures for example. Settings of individual device channels for sending measured values have priority.
*Time for a status message, if the status does not change:*
**(A+1) x (B+1) x C seconds**

Status messages are sent at this interval, even if the status has not changed since the last transmission. This can be used to check whether the device is within range / in operation

The following applies:

**A = Number of messages that are left out
B = Number of unchanged status messages that are left out
C = Random time between 120 and 184 seconds**

parameterHelp.MULTICAST_ROUTER_MODULE_ENABLED:
The 'Multicast Routing' function can be used to adapt the behaviour of the device in its function as a wireless router to extend the range. Multicast radio commands control the wireless communication partners simultaneously (i.e. in parallel). In this way it is possible to switch on several devices like lights at the same time. Afterwards all partners are serially (successively) addressed by unicast radio command. This results in an increased radio traffic at the router, which may lead to functional restrictions (duty cycle).

If the parameter is not activated, the sensors are always addressed individually one after the other, thus keeping the radio traffic low.

An exception are the Homematic IP Wall Thermostats. If they are connected to a switch actuator, the wall thermostats only send one multicast radio command at the same time. For a switch actuator to be used for heating control with a wireless router, this function must therefore be active.

We recommend the setting with deactivated parameters, unless this is necessary for the reasons mentioned above.

parameterHelp.REFERENCE_16BIT_MAX_SOIL_MOISTURE:
**Raw value-reference value for 100% soil moisture.**.

**Reference height**

Distance between the sensor and the reference point, which should be displayed as zero height. When mounted on a ceiling with the viewing direction toward the floor, the distance between the sensor and the floor is normally entered here.
parameterHelp.REPEAT_ENABLE:
If this check box is activated, the smoke alarm works as a repeater for wireless telegrams from other smoke alarms within the installation or group to increase the alerting range.

Telegrams that have already been repeated are not repeated again. It is therefore not possible to daisy chain repeaters.

This function is only intended to allow smoke alarms to communicate wirelessly with each other, so that remote smoke alarms can be reliably alerted even in case of power failure.
parameterHelp.REPETITIONOFFTIMEDIMMER: Select the pause between the repetitions with the off duration. If a permanent on-time or off-time is selected, the Repeats parameter is ignored.
parameterHelp.REPETITIONOFFTIMESOUND: Select the pause between the repetitions with the off duration. If a permanent off time is selected, the Repeats parameter is ignored.
parameterHelp.ROUTER_MODULE_ENABLED:
**The device acts as router**

This option allows the Homematic IP device to forward wireless commands. It therefore is used to increase the reach of standalone components.
parameterHelp.SAMPLES_PER_CYCLE: The device cyclically transmits the data every 2-3 minutes. If the transmission interval is too slow because e.g. a central control unit program is supposed to react faster, you can configure additional data requests per transmission interval relating to threshold values for deviation of power of both channels that trigger additional transmissions.
parameterHelp.SAMPLE_INTERVAL:
This value defines the time taken for checking door or window contacts (door/window open or closed).

The battery runtime is based on a scanning frequency of 0.5 seconds.By lengthening the time take, e.g., by reducing the scanning frequency to 1 second, the battery runtime can be greatly increased.

Depending on the application, it makes sense to lengthen the time taken. Whereas a longer scanning frequency is uncritical in a heating solution, the scanning frequency should be made shorter in a security solution for the alarm response.
parameterHelp.SAMPLE_INTERVAL_DOOR_STATE:
At the set interval, the door status sensor checks the magnetic field for changes, which then allows a change in door status to be detected.

A lower value shortens the response time but also increases the device's power consumption.
parameterHelp.SCREEN_MANAGEMENT:
***Screen Management***
Select the order in which the possible screens of the display are scrolled through here. After you have taught the display to the CCU, 1 screen is initially available. This is Screen 1. To activate further screens, proceed as follows:

For each screen there are 2 selection boxes, with which you can select the left and right neighboring screen respectively. This is indicated by the symbols < and >. To activate the second screen, for example, select the following as the right neighbor using the > selection box under Screen 1. To return from Screen 2 to Screen 1, activate the value 1 in the < selection box under Screen 2.
parameterHelp.SENSOR_SENSITIVITY:
When using as vibration sensor, this parameter can be used to set the sensor sensitivity. That means:

16G = very insensitive
8G
4G
2G
2G+
2G++ = very sensitive
parameterHelp.SENSOR_SENSITIVITY_DLP:
This parameter determines the sensitivity of the vibration monitoring.

A low value means low sensitivity, so that only strong vibrations are detected.

A high value means high sensitivity, so that even small vibrations are detected.

**Note: Vibration monitoring is only active when the door lock is locked.**
parameterHelp.SENSOR_SENSITIVITY_DOOR_LOCK:
Parameter for lock load detection.

During motorised locking, the mechanical resistance (torque) is measured. If the torque is lower than expected, this is reported as an error. This function is optional or can be used as an alternative to the door status sensor.

This function is only useful on doors where the torque is higher when the door is closed than when it is open. This function is therefore usually not usable if the latch already absorbs the force of the door seal.

A small value means low sensitivity, so that only stiff locks are detected. A large value means high sensitivity, so that even smooth-running locks are detected. At 255, the function is deactivated.

The parameter should be set about 3 lower than the measured value of a motorised locking movement with the door open. The measured value can be found under Status and Operation. A measured value of 255 means invalid.
parameterHelp.SENSOR_SENSITIVITY_RAIN:
You can adjust the rain sensor sensitivity here. A higher value implies higher sensitivity.

Setting 0%: Almost the entire sensor surface must be covered with rainwater for the sensor to trigger.

Setting 100%: A small drop (of approx. 70mm³) is sufficient to trigger the sensor (more or less, depending on the area).

**Please note:**
If drinking water is used for a test of the sensor, the amount of water required for triggering is reduced, as its conductance value is usually several potencies of 10 higher.
parameterHelp.SENSOR_SENSITIVITY_SHUTTERTRANS:
This parameter allows you to adjust the sensitivity of the obstacle detection or to disable it. It is recommended to start with the default setting.

If the roller shutter frequently stops without encountering an obstacle, the sensitivity of the obstacle detection system can be reduced. This should be done gradually. Similarly, the sensitivity can be increased if required.

parameterHelp.SPDR_CHANNEL_MODE:
- **1 - Inactive**
Deactivate counter-based switching of sensor
- **2 - Passage counting both directions**
If the desired number of passages is reached, the defined decision value will be sent and direct connections that react to this value are triggered.

In this mode, the sensor reacts to passages from both directions.
- **3 - Passage counting right to left**
Here, the same applies as for item 2. The sensor only reacts on passages from right to left.
- **4 - Passage counting left to right**
Here, also the same applies as for item 2. The sensor only reacts to passages from left to right.
- **5 -Difference of passages - left **
In this mode an internal counter variant is increased by 1 on detected passage to LEFT and reduced by 1 on passage detected to RIGHT. The mimium value of the internal counter variable is ZERO and the maximum value is 1000.

The adjustable upper and lower difference value is used to create a hysteresis. If the internal counter reaches the upper difference value, a switching command is send with the upper decision value to the connection partner(s). Additional passages are counted until the maximum value but will not cause additional switching commands. Only when reaching the lower difference value, a switching command with the lower decision value is sent to the connection partner(s).
- **6 -Difference of passages - right **
In this mode an internal counter variant is increased by 1 on detected passage to RIGHT and reduced by 1 on passage detected to LEFT. The mimium value of the internal counter variable is ZERO and the maximum value is 1000.

The adjustable upper and lower difference value is used to create a hysteresis. If the internal counter reaches the upper difference value, a switching command is send with the upper decision value to the connection partner(s). Additional passages are counted until the maximum value but will not cause additional switching commands. Only when reaching the lower difference value, a switching command with the lower decision value is sent to the connection partner(s).
parameterHelp.SPEED_SELECT_DOOR_STATE:
The door lock drive operates at the set speed if the auto-relock channel is activated.

Externally triggered movements include movements triggered by incoming commands or by pressing a button.

Self-triggered movements include auto-relock movements and movements triggered by the internal weekly programme.

The set speed can also be used without the auto-relock function by setting the *Wait time before auto-relock* to *Permanent* and *Automatic locking to Ignore door status* (channel 12).
parameterHelp.TEMPERATUREFALL_MODUS:
You can individually adjust the mode settings of the temperature
fall detection here.

- Inactive: Temperature fall detection inactive
- Auto mode: Temperature fall detection only active in auto mode
- Auto + manu mode: Temperature fall detection only active in auto and manu mode
- Active: Temperature fall detection active in all modes (default)
parameterHelp.TEMPERATUREFALL_WINDOW_OPEN_TIME_PERIOD:
You can adjust the duration of the temperature fall detection here.

This function is not possible in connection with a HomeMatic Window Contact.
parameterHelp.TEMPERATURE_OFFSET:
As the temperature is measured on the radiator, the temperature distribution can vary throughout a room. To adjust this, a temperature offset of ±3.5°C can be set.

If a temperature of e.g.18°C is measured instead of the set 20°C, an offset temperature of -2.0°C can be set. An offset temperature of 0.0°C is set in the factory settings.

You can individually adjust the offset temperature here.
parameterHelp.TEMPERATURE_OFFSET_STE2: The temperature is measured via two separate sensors. This results in a deviation in the temperature measured. For compensation, a temperature offset can be set here for the respective sensor. To do this, bring the sensors to the same temperature (wait a few minutes if necessary) and read the recorded values. The resulting deviation can be set as positive or negative offset for one of the channels.
parameterHelp.TRIGGER_ANGLE: When used as position detection sensor, this parameter determines by how many degrees the angle of the top/bottom of the sensor has to change in relation to the horizontal, to trigger an event.
parameterHelp.TRIGGER_ANGLE_2: When being used as a position detection sensor, this parameter determines by how many degrees the angle of the top/bottom side of the sensor must change in relation to the horizontal so that the vertical state is achieved.
parameterHelp.TRIGGER_ANGLE_DLP: This parameter determines by how many degrees the angle of the device must change in relation to the vertical in order for a position error to be detected.
parameterHelp.TRIGGER_ANGLE_HYSTERESIS:
Trigger angle hysteresis (+/-):

The limit for the next angle range must be exceeded by this amount in order to change to the state of the next angle range.
parameterHelp.TWO_POINT_HYSTERESIS:
In connection with a switch actuator, the room thermostat can be used as on-off control.

The on-off control depends on the setpoint and actual temperature as well as the defined hysteresis.
parameterHelp.TWO_POINT_HYSTERESIS_A:
In heating mode, the actuator switches on when the temperature falls below the setpoint temperature. In cooling mode, it is switched on when the setpoint temperature is exceeded.

The hysteresis can be used to control by how many K a reading must exceed or fall below the setpoint temperature for the actuator to switch off again.

This parameter is used to define the hysteresis in the range from 0.2 K to 2.0 K.
parameterHelp.TWO_POINT_HYSTERESIS_HUMIDITY:
In 'Humidify' mode, the actuator switches on when the air humidity falls below the set threshold. In 'Dry' mode, it is switched on when the set humidity threshold is exceeded.

The hysteresis can be used to control by how much % RH a reading must exceed or fall below the setpoint temperature for the actuator to switch off again.

This parameter is used to define the hysteresis in the range from 2 % to 20 %.
parameterHelp.VALVE_ERROR_RUN_POSITION:
If an empty battery has not been recognized, the radiator thermostat moves back into a "valve error position". This avoids, that the room temperature will cool down completely. A valve error position of 15 % is set in the factory settings.

You can individually adjust the value here (0 to 100 %).
parameterHelp.VALVE_MAXIMUM_POSITION:
A maximum valve opening of 100% is set in the factory settings.

You can individually adjust the maximum valve opening position
(0-100 %) here.
parameterHelp.VALVE_OFFSET:
If several radiators in one room are operated with a HomeMatic Radiator Thermostat some radiators may heat more than others. In certain cases, some radiators might be hot while others are still cold.

To compensate this, a valve offset can be set for the radiator thermostat that is mounted on the cold radiator. A valve offset of 0% is set in the factory settings.

You can individually adjust the value here (0 to 100 %).
parameterHelp.VOLTAGE_0:
Use this parameter to influence the output voltage.

Example: value of the output voltage when switched off (0 %):

50 % -> 5 V oder 10 % -> 1 V
parameterHelp.VOLTAGE_100:
Use this parameter to influence the output voltage.

Example: value of the output voltage when switched on (100 %):

100 % -> 10 V oder 50 % -> 5 V

uiLabels.dialogsettingsadvancedsettingshintsystem: Auto Backups: Creates automatic daily backups (at 00:07 am).
Mediola NEO-Server Autostartup: Upon startup of the CCU, the Mediola NEO server process will be automatically started if it has been activated in the configuration.
System name: Defines a custom name for this system that shows up in the browser title bar, tab and start page.

Security check (Portforwarding): To ensure, that no security critical portforwarding is enabled in the internet connectivity used, a regular check will be performed each sunday at 04:00 am. In case a critical portforwarding is identified an alarm message will be raised accordingly.
Check for additional software updates: Checks for new versions of additional software (ccu-addons) once a day and shows it on the startpage.
CloudMatic Autostartup: Upon startup of the CCU, the CloudMatic service will be automatically initialized and started if this is activated here.
IP address (HB-RF-ETH): If available the IP address of a HB-RF-ETH adapter can be configued here (requires reboot).

Protect from external internet access: If enabled, an additional local firewall protection for WebUI/services will be setup. If disabled, /etc/config/AllowExternalAccess will be set and the local firewall protection for direct internet access will be disabled.
Backup Storage Path: Storage location where automatic backups files (*.sbk) are stored. Default: connected USB media (when using a SD card as the central storage).
Backup Quantity (max.): Maximum number of backups to retain until older ones are purged (default: 30). Use 0 to disable automatic purge, keeping all backup data files.
Duty-Cycle system variables: System variables containing the duty cycle value for each rf interface are generated and updated periodically.
LED use (RF module): In case of using a RPI-RF-MOD/HmIP-CCU3 rf module or a HM-LGW-O-TW-W-EU the LED will be used to display alarm- oder service messages status.
LED use (Onboard): If the used system board (e.g. RaspberryPi, CCU3) comes with onboard LEDs they will be used to reflect the current system status.
Storage check (Bad Blocks): For checking the health status of the used system storage a check will be peformed each night at 01:59 am and in case bad blocks are found a WebUI alarm will be raised.
Storage check (FSTRIM): If activated, unused filesystem data will be freed each saturday at 04:00 am on supported system drives (e.g. SSD).
Custom Storage Path: As an alternative to the default of storing larger data to e.g. a connected USB drive, an own directory path can be entered here (requires reboot).
uiLabels.dialogsettingsadvancedsettingshintwatchd: Internet Monitoring: The internet connection will be regularly monitored and a WebUI alarm raised if an interruption is identified.

USB3 Monitoring (RaspberryPi4): A WebUI alarm will be raised if the system board is a RaspberryPi4 and a USB3 port (blue) is used together with a rf module connected to the GPIO bus. This combination is known to produce severe rf interferences which negatively affects communication with HomeMatic/homematicIP devices.

uiLabels.motiondetectorhelp: Selecting the transmission interval If the "Type of duration period" will be set to "minimal" (default) when creating a new direct device connection, the transmission interval will have immediate effect on the min. duration period of the consumer load (actuator). Then, the following relation applies: Set to classic: In this setting, the functions of a classical motion detector will apply. The transmission interval is set to 240 seconds (+ 10% tolerance). This means: The motion detector immediately informs about the first recognized movements newly recognized movements will be send again after about 240 seconds. In case of direct device connections, e.g. with a wireless switch (to switch on the lighting) the lighting will automatically be switched on for 5 minutes. Thus, the lighting will be switched off at earliest 5 minutes after the recognized movement. In case of continuous movement, the switch-on duration will automatically be extended by 5 minutes. Advantage: Pre-determined switch-on time of loads and stand-bye mode of motion detector. Disadvantage: Switch-on time shorter than 5 minutes impossible. Set to dynamic: The transmission interval will automatically adapt to the movement in the room. The minimum value can be adjusted. Please note, that smaller values will decrease the battery life. The motion detector immediately informs about the first recognized movements newly recognized movements will be send again after the entered minimum time (e.g. 30 seconds). In case of direct device connections, e.g. with a wireless switch (to switch on the lighting) the lighting will automatically be switched on for 30 seconds. The lighting will be switched off after 30 seconds. In case of continuous movement, the motion detector will automatically extend the transmission interval step-by-step (dynamic) and the switch-on duration of a directly connected device by up to 10 minutes. Advantage: For surroundings with little movements the switch-on time for directly connected devices can be kept short to save energy. Disadvantage: The switch-on time is unforeseeable and can take up to 10 minutes. Shortened battery life of motion detector.
